title: Source spec
description: The whole contract for one connector: what to fetch, how to page it, what is incremental, when it runs, and what 'arrived correctly' means. Nothing about a particular API is compiled into the runtime; anything this vocabulary cannot express goes in the connector's own extension.py.

name.description: Identity. Must equal the directory name; becomes raw_<name>, the dlt pipeline name, and the <name>_ingest/_backfill/_reconcile DAG ids.

status.description: connected = DAGs are generated and live, and the token is demanded on every clone. reference = validated and built by the test harness but scheduled by nothing. paused = DAGs exist with no schedule. Required with no default: scheduling a connector must be a deliberate line in a reviewable diff.

owner.description: Who to ask when this connector breaks. Free text; surfaced in the generated inventory.

rate_limits.description: Requests per minute per endpoint family. The pacer spreads requests across these proactively, so 429s stay rare rather than being recovered from.

extensions.description: true when this connector ships an extension.py beside its spec. The loader derives the path, so there is no module name to drift. A string is the legacy spelling and is accepted with a deprecation warning.

type.description: Registered auth builders. `extension` hands auth construction to the connector's own extension.py, for schemes no generic builder covers (request signing, rotating HMAC).

token_env.description: The NAME of the environment variable holding the credential — never the credential. This is what lets a spec live in a public repo.

schedule.description: Cron for the ingest DAG, or null for manual only. Pick a minute clear of the other connectors' — `ingest validate` warns on collisions.

reconcile.description: Cron for the full-history re-fetch that tombstones deletions. Only builds a DAG together with backfill_start.

pool.description: Airflow pool. Defaults to <name>_pipeline — one slot, so a source's runs cannot race their own incremental cursor.

backfill_start.description: The floor of this source's history. Required for a reconcile DAG: the tombstone pass is only safe on a run that provably covered all of history, and this is what it compares against.

runtime.description: Task-size tier. Read by the DAG generator and by terraform when sizing this source's ephemeral task. light = rate-limit-bound API pulls; standard = fan-out sources and most backfills; long = multi-hour paced reads; heavy = large snapshots and anything holding rows in memory.

pagination.description: Source-wide paging defaults. A resource may override any of it under endpoint.paginator / endpoint.data_selector.

data_selector.description: Where the records live in the response envelope. Source-wide default only — APIs whose envelope differs per endpoint set it per resource instead.

paginator.description: A registered shorthand, a dlt paginator name, or a raw dlt paginator config passed through untouched.

primary_key.description: The merge key. Identity checks (not null, unique) are generated from it and are never opt-in.

write_disposition.description: merge is the default and the safe one: a re-fetched row updates in place. append cannot dedupe, so a run killed mid-load can duplicate rows — `ingest validate` requires a justification comment for it.

soft_delete.description: When absence from a run is allowed to mean 'deleted upstream'. always = the resource is fully re-fetched every run. full_history = only a run that covered all of history may tombstone. Never a bare boolean.

hint_columns.description: Columns dlt must type deterministically because something compares them. Defaults to every timestamp column.

promote.description: {'nested.path': 'column'} — the only nested scalars that become real columns. Everything else is JSON-stringified, so a new upstream field cannot mint a column or a child table.

html_text.description: {'html_field': 'text_column'} — strip markup into a companion column.

data_selector.description: Per-resource override of the envelope path, for APIs that wrap each endpoint differently.

cursor_path.description: Per-resource override of where the next-page cursor lives in the response.

cursor_param.description: Per-resource override of the query parameter carrying the next-page cursor.

params.description: Query parameters sent on every request to this endpoint.

json.description: Body sent with a POST endpoint.

page_size_param.description: Spelling of the page-size parameter. `limit` is only the most common one, not a universal one.

family.description: Rate-limit family. Defaults to the resource name, so a source that does not group its endpoints gets one budget each.

strategy.description: The fetch algorithm. full_refresh and cursor are built declaratively and need no Python; the other three name an algorithm the connector's extension.py must supply.

cursor_field.description: The record field the cursor tracks (dlt's cursor_path).

cursor_param.description: cursor strategy: the query parameter carrying the lower bound.

end_param.description: cursor strategy: the query parameter carrying the upper bound, for APIs that want a closed range.

initial_value.description: cursor strategy: where the first run starts. Absent means the API's own beginning.

lookback_seconds.description: Re-read this much already-loaded history on every run. Free under merge, and it covers records written while the previous run was mid-fetch.

parent.description: parent_* strategies: the resource whose rows drive this one's worklist.

window.description: search_window: the backfill endpoint and how wide a slice it will answer.

search.description: search_window: the incremental endpoint filtering on update time.

skip_statuses.description: parent_watermark: HTTP statuses meaning 'this parent is gone' — skip it rather than fail the run over a record that no longer exists.

budget_minutes.description: parent_watermark: wall-clock budget, so a long worklist stops cleanly and the next run resumes rather than being killed mid-load.

quality.description: What 'arrived correctly' means. Identity checks (primary key not null, unique, at least one row) are generated for every resource and are not declared here — everything in this block is in addition to them.

required.description: Tables whose absence is a hard failure rather than a quiet skip.

freshness.description: How recently the SOURCE last changed a record. Advisory by default: on a quiet weekend it fails while the pipeline is healthy. One entry, or several for a source with more than one clock.

max_deleted_fraction.description: A run tombstoning more than this share of a table means the soft-delete predicate misfired.
